policy_title: Raise School Standards and Recruit Teachers
stated: Labour will raise school standards by improving numeracy and funding evidence-based early-language interventions in primary schools. They will recruit an additional 6,500 expert teachers, review bursary allocation and retention payments, update the Early Career Framework, and introduce a Teacher Training Entitlement. The School Support Staff Negotiating Body will be reinstated. Funding for these measures will come from ending the VAT exemption and business rates relief for private schools.

source.quote: Labour is determined to raise school standards for every child, and ensure they are prepared for the future. Most children attend schools where the Conservatives are failing to provide the support and teaching that they need. Raising school standards starts with early education. We will do the same for numeracy, improving the quality of maths teaching across nurseries and primary schools. Developing early communication skills is another key foundation for life, with serious knock-on consequences when development is delayed. Labour will fund evidence-based early-language interventions in primary schools, so that every child can find their voice. Labour will end the VAT exemption and business rates relief for private schools to invest in our state schools. Labour will recruit an additional 6,500 new expert teachers. We will get more teachers into shortage subjects, support areas that face recruitment challenges, and tackle retention issues. The way bursaries are allocated, and the structure of retention payments, will be reviewed. We will update the Early Career Framework, maintaining its grounding in evidence, and ensure any new teacher entering the classroom has, or is working towards, Qualified Teacher Status. We will introduce a new Teacher Training Entitlement to ensure teachers stay up to date on best practice with continuing professional development. School support staff play a vital role in children’s education and development. Labour will reinstate the School Support Staff Negotiating Body, which will help address the acute recruitment and retention crisis in support roles.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets school standards, early-language interventions, teacher recruitment and training — all core indicators of education quality and opportunity.

Reinstating the School Support Staff Negotiating Body and introducing a Teacher Training Entitlement materially affect pay, conditions, and job security for a large workforce of school staff and teachers.

The funding mechanism (removing VAT exemption and business rates relief from private schools, used predominantly by higher-income families) and redirecting receipts to state school improvements constitutes a redistribution that could narrow the educational attainment gap and downstream income inequality — a concrete mechanism bearing on O14.

membership_note: Three bearings: O7 is the core designed-for outcome; O4 arises from the support-staff bargaining body and teacher pay/retention reforms; O14 arises from the redistributive funding mechanism (private-to-state). Fiscal sustainability (O12) was considered but the policy explicitly cites a specific revenue source, and the uncertainty over whether VAT receipts meet projections is a projection-tier dispute rather than a clear structural worsening of the debt path. O13 (long-run productivity) was considered but is too indirect and long-horizon to earn a non-negligible verdict distinct from O7.
